name: Aulua
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Ray 1926 Grammar of the Aulua language READ in full (Rosetta/archive.org rosettaproject_aul_morsyn-1): alphabet+morphosyntax only, no stress or accent statement; Ray 1893 sketch unlikely to add one.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1893. Sketch of Aulua grammar, with vocabularies of Aulua and Lamangkau, Malekula, New Hebrides. Journal of the Anthropological Institute 22: 386-397.
sources.note: Sec. I 'Alphabet' (p. 387) gives vowel/consonant values ('The vowels have the Italian sound'), optional prenasalisation and Aulua~Pangkumu sound correspondences; no remark on accent or stress anywhere in the sketch (page image read; scanned grep for accent/stress/syllable empty).

sources.citation: Birchfield, Alexandra & Elizabeth Pearce. 2021. Syllable prominence in Unua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 39.
sources.note: About neighbouring Unua (phrase-level penultimate pitch prominence). Its pp. 1-2 survey of every published stress statement for Malakula languages (Tape, Naman, Neve'ei, Neverver, Unua, Avava, Tirax, Ahamb, Nahavaq) does not mention Aulua - indirect evidence that no Aulua stress statement was in print as of 2021.

sources.citation: Lynch, John. 2020. The phonological history of Uripiv, an Eastern Malakula language. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia 38.
sources.note: Cites Aulua forms only as comparanda; no statement about Aulua stress.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva et al. 2015-2016. Aulua wordlists (Loxse-Asolokh, Loxse-Lanfitfit, Netimb; Tesmbol Usus/Melaklak) in ABVD and Vanuatu Voices (vanuatuvoices.clld.org, MPI-EVA).
sources.note: Broad IPA transcriptions with audio; 0 of 923 ABVD forms and 0 of 185 Vanuatu Voices forms carry a stress mark; no prose statement.

sources.citation: Paviour-Smith, Martin & Willy Makenzie. 2005. Exacting the hen's revenge: an initial enquiry into the nature of narrative in Aulua. Wellington Working Papers in Linguistics 17: 59-73.
sources.note: Discourse/narrative structure only; nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Paviour-Smith, Martin. 2005. Mood marking on Malakula. Wellington Working Papers in Linguistics 17: 43-58.
sources.note: Sec. 3.2 'Aulua' describes realis/irrealis initial-consonant mutation and the orthography (<h>, <q>, <nr>); no stress statement (scanned grep stress/accent/penult empty).

sources.citation: Lynch, John & Terry Crowley. 2001. Languages of Vanuatu: a new survey and bibliography. Pacific Linguistics 517. Sec. 3.7.12 Aulua, pp. 77-78.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6211.V36 L96 2001
sources.note: Bibliographic survey: lists Ray 1893, Ray 1926:273-283, Tryon 1976 wordlist, Charpentier 1982b vocabulary, and unpublished Paviour-Smith field data as the totality of Aulua materials; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1926. Grammar of the Aulua language. In: A comparative study of the Melanesian island languages, 273-283. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.
sources.note: Secs. 1-2 'Alphabet'/'Sounds' (pp. 273-274): 'Vowels as in Italian', consonant values, nasalised consonants 'apparently at the choice of the speaker'; nothing on accent/stress. Rest is morphosyntax (confirms earlier scan).

sources.citation: Grambank v1, language aulu1238 (coded from Ray 1893:387 and Ray 1926:274 only).
sources.note: Confirms no modern grammar was available to Grambank coders; no stress information.

sources.citation: Paviour-Smith, Martin (Massey University). Unpublished Aulua field materials / grammar notes (fieldwork 2001-2005 onward, cited by Lynch & Crowley 2001, Crowley 2006, Lynch 2016).
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: The only modern descriptive work on Aulua; any phonology chapter would contain the stress statement. Could be requested from the author.

sources.citation: Shimelman, Aviva; Heggarty, Paul; Walworth, Mary et al. 2019-2020. Vanuatu Voices (vanuatuvoices.clld.org): Aulua doculects Loxse-Asolokh, Loxse-Lanfitfit, Netimb with audio (c. 185 items each); also Charpentier's Aulua tapes VKS-149_26 (PARADISEC/VKS).

sources.note: Open audio that would allow a quick instrumental/auditory determination of stress placement in the absence of any published statement.
